l4_steps.name: Retrieve active flight plan from flight planning system
l4_steps.input: Scheduled departure, route database, aircraft tail assignment
l4_steps.output: Draft Operational Flight Plan (OFP) with route, altitude, and estimated fuel
l4_steps.kpi: Flight plan available ≥60 min before STD; plan accuracy within ±2% of actual fuel burn
l4_steps.pain_point: NAVBLUE integration latency with ATC slot data can delay plan finalization for constrained airspace; manual re-route required for TFR-affected corridors

l4_steps.name: Pull METAR, TAF, SIGMET and PIREP weather data
l4_steps.input: Departure, destination, and alternate ICAO codes; planned departure time
l4_steps.output: Consolidated weather package including en-route SIGMET and PIREP overlays
l4_steps.kpi: Weather package delivered ≤45 min before STD; SIGMET currency ≤6 hrs
l4_steps.pain_point: SIGMETs for en-route convection update every 4–6 hrs; late-breaking convective SIGMETs may not be captured before release window, requiring mid-dispatch reassessment

l4_steps.name: Assess weather at origin, destination and alternate
l4_steps.input: Weather package, airline published operating minima, alternate requirements
l4_steps.output: Weather go/no-go recommendation with alternate aerodrome confirmed
l4_steps.kpi: Destination forecast visibility and ceiling at or above published CAT I/II/III minima at ETA
l4_steps.pain_point: Rapid deterioration below CAT II minima at destination with simultaneous weather impact on primary alternate forces late alternate change, disrupting fuel calculation and ATC filing

l4_steps.name: Calculate fuel uplift including contingency and alternate
l4_steps.input: Route fuel burn, wind data, alternate distance, company fuel policy, EDCT delay estimate
l4_steps.output: Minimum regulatory fuel figure plus discretionary uplift recommendation
l4_steps.kpi: Planned fuel ≥ FAR 121.645 / ICAO Annex 6 minimum (trip + 5% contingency + alternate + 30 min final reserve); fuel overage ≤3% of trip fuel
l4_steps.pain_point: EDCT ground delay burn estimates from FAA TFMS are systematically optimistic; dispatcher must manually add 10–15% buffer for GDP-affected departures, yet excess uplift increases fuel cost by ~$8/kg

l4_steps.name: File IFR flight plan with ATC via AFTN/SITA
l4_steps.input: Finalized OFP route, departure time, aircraft type and registration, SELCAL
l4_steps.output: Filed FPL message (ICAO format) acknowledged by ATC; filing receipt stored
l4_steps.kpi: Flight plan filed ≥30 min before EOBT; filing acknowledgment received ≤5 min
l4_steps.pain_point: EUROCONTROL NM slot allocation (CTOT) can force departure time change ≤2 hrs before departure, requiring immediate re-file and downstream fuel/crew duty recalculation

l4_steps.name: Confirm ATC slot/EDCT and assess crew duty impact
l4_steps.input: Filed FPL, GDP/AFP program data, crew duty time records from Jeppesen Crew Management
l4_steps.output: Confirmed CTOT/EDCT, updated STD, crew duty compliance confirmation
l4_steps.kpi: EDCT compliance rate ≥98%; crew duty limit breach rate <0.5% of dispatched flights
l4_steps.pain_point: Ground Delay Programs (GDPs) can shift EDCT by 60–180 min, pushing ATD past crew rest trigger thresholds under FAR Part 117; late crew swap triggers cascading downstream cancellations

l4_steps.name: Select and file alternate aerodrome with fuel coverage
l4_steps.input: Destination TAF, alternate airport ops and NOTAM status, fuel range envelope
l4_steps.output: Filed alternate ICAO code with calculated alternate fuel and regulatory compliance confirmed
l4_steps.kpi: Alternate meets FAR 121.619 one-hour TAF forecast above alternate minima at ETA ±1 hr
l4_steps.pain_point: Popular alternates (e.g. ORD when MDW is destination) can become simultaneously weather-affected; dispatcher must identify second-order alternates increasing fuel requirement and potentially triggering MTOW constraint

l4_steps.name: Check aircraft airworthiness status in MRO system
l4_steps.input: Tail number, scheduled departure, inbound tech log entries
l4_steps.output: Airworthiness confirmation or open deferred defect list with MEL references
l4_steps.kpi: Aircraft status confirmed ≥90 min before STD; zero open airworthiness directives beyond MEL tolerance
l4_steps.pain_point: Late squawks logged by inbound crew within 45 min of departure may not propagate to AMOS before the dispatch review window closes, creating undocumented MEL exposure

l4_steps.name: Review MEL and CDL items for dispatch acceptability
l4_steps.system: AMOS by Swiss AviationSoftware + Boeing Toolbox
l4_steps.input: Open deferred defects, current MEL/CDL revision, route and operating conditions
l4_steps.output: MEL dispatch determination (go/no-go) with any operational restrictions documented
l4_steps.kpi: MEL review completed ≤60 min before STD; zero dispatches with expired MEL interval items
l4_steps.pain_point: Cat B/C MEL items may impose altitude, fuel, or route restrictions that are not automatically propagated to NAVBLUE OFP, requiring manual dispatcher override and re-calculation

l4_steps.name: Verify V-speeds and performance for current configuration
l4_steps.input: Aircraft weight, MEL-driven configuration restrictions, runway condition report (SNOWTAM/RCR)
l4_steps.output: Confirmed V1/VR/V2, flap setting, derate selection, and balanced field length
l4_steps.kpi: Performance calculations completed ≤45 min before STD; all V-speeds within aircraft flight manual limits
l4_steps.pain_point: Contaminated runway friction coefficients (SNOWTAM data) may be up to 2 hrs old; dispatcher must verify runway treatment status with station ops before confirming RTOW, as stale data can overstate runway performance by 8–12%

l4_steps.name: Receive preliminary load figures from load control
l4_steps.input: Booked passenger count, checked baggage manifest, cargo booking, crew count
l4_steps.output: Preliminary Zero Fuel Weight (ZFW) and estimated Takeoff Weight (TOW)
l4_steps.kpi: Preliminary load sheet received ≥60 min before STD; ZFW variance from final ≤500 lbs
l4_steps.pain_point: Late connecting passengers and ad-hoc cargo add-ons can shift ZFW by 500–2,000 lbs after the initial fuel calculation, invalidating the filed fuel figure and requiring dispatch release amendment

l4_steps.name: Calculate final takeoff weight and CG envelope
l4_steps.input: Final passenger count, actual baggage weights by zone, hold cargo manifest, ballast
l4_steps.output: Final load sheet with confirmed TOW, ZFW, CG position as percentage of MAC
l4_steps.kpi: CG within ±2% MAC of certified envelope limits; TOW ≤ MTOW; load sheet issued ≤40 min before STD
l4_steps.pain_point: Bulk cargo density variances and last-minute bag pulls can cause CG exceedance not detected until ramp loading check, requiring hold reload that delays departure by 20–45 min

l4_steps.name: Perform runway-limited weight and obstacle clearance check
l4_steps.input: Final TOW, runway conditions, OAT, pressure altitude, obstacle departure procedure
l4_steps.output: Confirmed Regulated Takeoff Weight (RTOW), required field length, net takeoff flight path
l4_steps.kpi: Net takeoff flight path clears obstacles by ≥35 ft per FAR 121.189; RTOW ≥ actual TOW
l4_steps.pain_point: High-elevation airports (DEN 5,431 ft, SLC 4,227 ft) combined with high OAT frequently trigger weight restrictions that were not anticipated in the original schedule, forcing payload offload decisions at gate

l4_steps.name: Generate Operational Flight Plan and dispatch release
l4_steps.input: Final fuel uplift, confirmed load sheet, MEL notes, weather package, NOTAM summary
l4_steps.output: Completed Operational Flight Plan (OFP) and unsigned Dispatch Release document
l4_steps.kpi: OFP issued ≥30 min before EOBT; NOTAM safety-critical items highlighted in release
l4_steps.pain_point: NOTAM volumes at major hubs can exceed 150 active NOTAMs per airport; dispatcher must manually filter safety-critical items, creating fatigue-driven oversight risk without automated NOTAM triage tooling

l4_steps.name: Brief Captain on route, weather, NOTAMs and MEL status
l4_steps.system: SITA ACARS / Telex (or face-to-face at hub)
l4_steps.input: OFP, weather package, NOTAM summary, MEL items, EDCT/CTOT, fuel figure
l4_steps.output: Completed crew briefing record with dispatcher and captain acknowledgement
l4_steps.kpi: Crew briefing completed ≥20 min before EOBT; briefing acknowledgment logged in dispatch system
l4_steps.pain_point: At remote outstations, dispatcher-captain contact via ACARS can be disrupted by ground power failures; fallback to VHF voice briefing must be documented under FAR 121.663 joint responsibility

l4_steps.name: Captain reviews and co-signs Dispatch Release (FAR 121.663)
l4_steps.system: SITA ACARS (electronic signature) or paper release
l4_steps.input: Dispatch Release document, OFP, fuel order, weather and NOTAM briefing package
l4_steps.output: Dual-signed Dispatch Release (dispatcher + captain) confirming joint airworthiness decision
l4_steps.kpi: Release co-signed ≤15 min before EOBT; 100% of departures have dual-signed release on file
l4_steps.pain_point: Under FAR 121, dispatch is a joint captain-dispatcher decision; captain fuel uplift amendments after signing trigger full release re-issue, consuming 10–20 min and risking EDCT miss

l4_steps.name: Issue final dispatch release and transmit to crew
l4_steps.input: Co-signed Dispatch Release, confirmed fuel order, updated departure time
l4_steps.output: Transmitted final release; flight authorized to depart; release archived in dispatch system
l4_steps.kpi: Release transmitted ≥10 min before EOBT; 100% compliance; ACARS delivery confirmation within 2 min
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS datalink failures at remote outstations require fallback to voice release per FAR 121.663; voice releases must be manually transcribed and archived, creating audit trail gaps if not logged within 1 hr

l4_steps.name: Monitor departure, pushback and initial climb confirmation
l4_steps.input: ATC off-blocks clearance, pushback notification from ramp, ACARS OUT message
l4_steps.output: Confirmed actual off-blocks time (AOBT); flight tracker status updated to airborne
l4_steps.kpi: AOBT recorded within 2 min of actual event; D0 (on-time departure) target ≥78%
l4_steps.pain_point: AMS/Altéa PSS timestamp synchronization errors can misreport AOBT by 3–8 min, causing downstream crew duty time calculations to use incorrect start-of-duty reference under FAR Part 117

l4_steps.name: Track flight en-route via ACARS position reports
l4_steps.input: Automatic ACARS position reports (15-min intervals), ATC radar handoff confirmations
l4_steps.output: Updated ETA, fuel-remaining trend, en-route deviation log, revised destination weather check
l4_steps.kpi: Position report gap ≤15 min; fuel remaining vs. plan within ±500 lbs at each waypoint
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS blackout over oceanic tracks (no VHF/SATCOM backup) leaves dispatcher without real-time fuel data for up to 60 min; oceanic fuel emergencies cannot be detected until HF radio contact is re-established

l4_steps.name: Initiate diversion or emergency response if required
l4_steps.input: In-flight emergency notification, medical diversion request, fuel emergency, weather deterioration below minima
l4_steps.output: Diversion airport selected with fuel coverage confirmed; ATC coordination initiated; ground support activated at diversion airport
l4_steps.kpi: Diversion decision communicated to crew ≤5 min from trigger event; ground support activated ≤15 min before ETA at diversion
l4_steps.pain_point: Diversion airports at unplanned stations may lack MEL-required spare parts or certified line maintenance capability, extending AOG time by 4–24 hrs and triggering cascading schedule disruption across the network
